questions.text: "She ___ across the room when she ___ a voice she recognised." Choose the correct forms.
questions.hint: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption)

questions.text: "The lights ___ and the room ___ of old wood and rain." (Scene-setting)
questions.hint: Past continuous for ongoing scene + past simple for state

questions.text: "She ___ (never / visit) that part of the city before that night."
questions.hint: Past perfect for event/state before the narrative moment

questions.text: "No sooner ___ she ___ (arrive) than the meeting was called to order."
questions.hint: "No sooner had + subject + pp… than"

questions.text: "___ had he felt so exposed." (Dramatic inversion)
opts: All of the above are correct
questions.correct: All of the above are correct
questions.hint: Never / not once / rarely + had + subject + pp

questions.text: "By the time they ___ (reach) the shelter, the storm ___ (already / begin)."
questions.hint: "By the time" + past simple; earlier event = past perfect

questions.text: "___, outside, someone was watching the house." (Same time, different location)
questions.hint: "Meanwhile" = simultaneous action elsewhere

questions.text: Which is "showing" not "telling"?
opts: His hands were shaking as he read the letter.
questions.correct: His hands were shaking as he read the letter.
questions.hint: Showing = emotion expressed through physical action/detail

questions.text: "___, she placed the envelope on the table and walked out." (Manner adverb fronted)
questions.hint: Manner adverb at the front = emphasis on how the action was done

questions.text: "She ___ (wait) for three hours by the time he finally appeared." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: Past perfect continuous = ongoing action before narrative present

questions.text: The "inciting incident" is best described as…
opts: The event that starts the story moving
questions.correct: The event that starts the story moving
questions.hint: Reading 1: "sets the whole story in motion"

questions.text: "Without warning, ___." Which correctly uses this phrase?
questions.hint: "Without warning" + past simple = sudden action

questions.text: "She opens the door and steps inside" in a past narrative is a tense consistency error.
questions.hint: Present tense in a past narrative = tense slip

questions.text: What does "pacing" mean in narrative writing?
opts: The number of characters in a story
The speed at which the narrative moves
questions.correct: The speed at which the narrative moves
questions.hint: Reading 1: "pacing — the speed at which the narrative moves"

questions.text: Which correctly uses dramatic inversion?
opts: She never had felt so frightened.
Never she had felt so frightened.
Never had she felt so frightened.
Had never she felt so frightened.
questions.correct: Never had she felt so frightened.
questions.hint: Never + had + subject + past participle

questions.text: "He sat down. He ___ his hands together. He waited." (= joined/clasped — complete the sequence)
questions.hint: Past simple sequence of main actions

questions.text: "She had grown up here. ___ she felt like a stranger." (= contrast with the past)
questions.hint: "Now" shifts from past perfect backstory back to narrative present

questions.text: Which is a "compression sentence"?
opts: She heard every word he said and remembered each one.
He was walking slowly, looking at every window.
She felt the cold air on her face.
questions.hint: Compression = skipping time quickly in one short sentence

questions.text: "Not once ___ he ___ (apologise) for what he had done."
questions.hint: "Not once + did + subject + bare infinitive"

questions.text: According to the lectures, what does a strong narrative closing do?
opts: Echoes the opening or shifts the reader's understanding
Ends with the main character leaving
questions.correct: Echoes the opening or shifts the reader's understanding
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Ms. Aldanova on closings

questions.text: "While she was talking, he ___ quietly towards the door." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: "While" + past continuous; the other action = past simple

questions.text: Starting a narrative in the middle of the action is called starting "in ___ ___."
questions.hint: Latin phrase from Listening 3

questions.text: "There, ___ the window, stood a figure she had not seen in years." (= fronted place phrase)
questions.hint: Place fronted phrase with "there": "There, by the window, stood…"

questions.text: The past continuous is described as the "workhorse" of narrative — carrying the main events forward.
questions.hint: Reading 2: past simple is the "workhorse"

questions.text: A narrator who distorts events deliberately or unconsciously is called…
questions.hint: Reading 1: "unreliable narrator"
